name: Andorra
summary_text: Andorra is exceptionally safe for trans visitors. The 2022 Law of the Person and Family modernised the legal framework (unified civil marriage, and legal gender recognition provisions); the Ministry of Equality now obliges all companies to maintain sexual and gender-based harassment protocols. ILGA-Europe records only three bias-motivated incidents in the most recent annual review — a tiny absolute number reflecting a small, safe, tourism-dependent country. No traveler-facing concerns: no bathroom laws, no border issues (open border with Spain/France, though outside Schengen there are no document-gender checks), high social tolerance in practice despite a conservative Catholic history. Gaps: anti-discrimination coverage of gender identity is recent and shallower than Spain's; hate-crime law is generic rather than SOGI-specific. Caveat: very small population — the evidence base is thin, so this assessment carries greater-than-usual uncertainty.

sources.claim_summary: ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2024 (covering 2023) chapter on Andorra. The 2022 Law of the Person and Family entered into force in February 2023, introducing legal gender recognition. A newspaper opinion piece linking trans identities to mental illness was removed after protest, with a public apology. DiversAnd met the Health Ministry on gender-affirming care protocols following the 2022 regulatory changes; microaggressions were reported but rarely to authorities, attributed to fear.

ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2026 (covering 2025) chapter on Andorra. Police record an average of two to three bias-motivated incidents per month; DiversAnd calls for a formal hate-crime registration system. In October a decree on trans-specific healthcare entered into force: HRT via the social security system from age 16, surgery from 18, and consultation coverage for under-16s. New workplace harassment protocols were criticised for not explicitly addressing gender diversity or trans-specific harassment.

sources.title: Andorra's prime minister Xavier Espot Zamora,comes out as gay
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (Sept 2023): Andorra's prime minister Xavier Espot Zamora came out as gay ('I never hid it'), saying he hoped it shows young people that anyone can 'reach the highest magistracy'; during his premiership Andorra legalised same-sex marriage, introduced gender identity/expression anti-discrimination laws, and trans rights.
